notes: No official web page listing the byways was verified. The official list is administrative rule R926-13 (adminrules.utah.gov, not fetched). utah.com is a commercial site, not the state, so it was not used; the state tourism guide is a PDF on travel.utah.gov. GIS: UDOT 'Utah Scenic Byways' polyline (NAME, RANK National/State, ADOPTED_DATE, MILES), published on UDOT's Digital Delivery hub. It has 33 names, including Energy Loop extension segments and both 'Zion National Scenic Byway' and 'Zion Park Scenic Byway'. A UGRC copy also exists (UDOTMap_ScenicByways).

agency: Vermont Agency of Transportation (VTrans); designations by the Vermont Transportation Board
notes: The old program site vermont-byways.us no longer resolves (DNS failure) and no current VTrans program page was found (VTrans hosts only the Byways Program Manual PDF). The official state tourism page (https://www.vermontvacation.com/byways redirects here) lists 10 byways. It calls them 'federally designated', which is wrong: only Connecticut River is national; the rest are state byways. Byway links go to local or chamber sites. GIS: VTrans 'Scenic Byways' polyline, but its only attribute SCENICBYWAY holds numeric codes (100-1000), not names, so a code-to-name join is needed (not documented in the layer).

program: Virginia Byways (State Scenic Highway and Virginia Byways Act, 1966)
agency: Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT), with the Department of Conservation and Recreation; designations by the Commonwealth Transportation Board
notes: Virginia Byways are mostly unnamed route segments (3,500+ miles) shown on a map, not a named list. The page names only the national designations under 'three All American Roads and two National Scenic Byways'; just these four appeared in the page text, and The Journey Through Hallowed Ground is the likely fifth (unverified). GIS: 'Virginia's Byways' layer (Byways_022024, VDOT ArcGIS Online org) is the one behind the page's interactive map (experience 06a8ec8f96804c1cbf83c7f5bc5396e0); attributes are LRS route fields (RTE_NM etc.), not byway names. A DCR-hosted 'VDOT_Virginia_Scenic_Byways' layer also exists (services1.arcgis.com/PxUNqSbaWFvFgHnJ).

program: Washington State Scenic and Recreational Highways / Scenic Byways
agency: Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT), Local Programs
notes: No current WSDOT page listing the byways was found: the old URL www.wsdot.wa.gov/localprograms/scenicbyways/ now redirects to a generic 'Support local programs' page. Program set up under the 1967 Scenic and Recreational Highway Act. GIS: WSDOT 'Scenic Byways' polyline (fields RouteID, Designation = 'Scenic Highway' / 'Scenic Areas Designated', Description = segment limits such as 'JCT SR 101 VIC HOQUIAM TO TAHOLAH'). It covers the statutory Scenic and Recreational Highway segments and has no named-byway field (e.g. no 'Cascade Loop'), so names need a separate source.

agency: West Virginia Department of Transportation (WVDOT) / Division of Highways, with West Virginia Tourism
notes: No official page with the list was found: the wvtourism.com 'West Virginia Byways & Backways' page is a business-listing stub with no route names, and WVDOH's resources page has no byway links. GIS: WVDOT_Publisher 'Byways and Backways 2019' polyline (NAME, DESIGNATIO = National Scenic Byway / State Byway / State Backway). It appears incomplete: 17 names (Back Mountain, Camp Allegheny, Cedar Creek Road, Cheat Mountain, Cheat River, Coal Heritage Trail, Farm Heritage Road, George Washington Heritage Trail, Highland Scenic Highway, Little Kanawha Parkway, Mountain's Shadow Trail, Northwestern Turnpike, Old Route 7, Rich Mountain, Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike, Wellsburg-Bethany, Williams River), and it lacks e.g. Midland Trail and the National Road. WVDOT also has a 'Scenic Byway POI' point layer.

agency: Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT)
notes: 5 state-designated byways (Great River Road is an All-American Road; Door County Coastal and Lake Superior are National Scenic Byways). The page also lists USFS byways (Great Divide, Heritage Drive) under 'Other scenic byways', excluded here. Rustic Roads is a separate WisDOT program (126 local roads), not byways. Byway links go to local sites, and there is a WisDOT StoryMap. GIS: WisDOT 'Scenic Byways' polyline (BYWAY field, 5 names).

program: Wyoming Scenic Byways and Backways Program
agency: Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT)
notes: The WYDOT page only links brochures (Big Horn Scenic Byway, Buffalo Bill - Yellowstone Country Scenic Byway, Centennial Scenic Byway, Mirror Lake Scenic Byway & Big Spring Scenic Backway, Snowy Range Scenic Byway, plus a backways brochure) and a 2009 program book PDF. It has no full list, so byways left empty. The parent page https://dot.state.wy.us/home/travel/scenic_byways.html features Chief Joseph Scenic Byway. Two tiers: Byways and Backways. No WYDOT byway GIS layer found.
